definition: The auditory pathway is the set of nerve routes that carry sound-related signals through the brainstem, extending from the auditory nerve toward the mesencephalon. In this packet, it is described in the context of testing how well these pathways are functioning.

provenance.scope: Source record C184949; pinned source text

reasons: The packet is for the diagnostic procedure “Auditory Brainstem Response,” not the anatomical structure “auditory pathway,” so the requested sense is wrong.
The definition’s opening sentence reframes the packet as the nerve routes themselves; the packet instead defines an objective test of auditory brainstem function and auditory pathway function.
The claim that the packet describes the term “in the context of testing how well these pathways are functioning” is not a supported definition of the term and overstates what the source says.
The packet text defines/uses “Auditory Brainstem Response” as a diagnostic test/procedure, not as a definition of the anatomical construct “auditory pathway” as “the set of nerve routes.”

The packet supports that the measurement is “from the auditory nerve to the mesencephalon,” but it does not explicitly state that the “auditory pathway” is “the set of nerve routes” carrying “sound-related signals” through the brainstem.

Because the packet describes a test used to diagnose abnormalities of the 8th cranial nerve and associated auditory pathways, the provided definition may be conflating the procedure (auditory brainstem response) with the underlying pathways, which is not directly supported by the packet.
